search.doc:
Task 1 - Vector search (the job a vector database does).

Dataset   Fashion-MNIST, 60 000 x 784 indexed, 1 000 test-set queries.
Task      top-10 nearest neighbours by cosine similarity.
Truth     exact brute-force top-10 (numpy, float64).
Metric    recall@10; single-query latency p50/p95 over HTTP; index build time.

HeatherDB  plain-mode database, every vector a document; `documents/query`.
Qdrant     the real server (Docker, pinned image), cosine, default HNSW
           (m=16, ef_construct=100), REST API, default search params.

discovery.doc:
Task 2 - Pattern discovery (the job a clustering / segmentation job does).

Dataset   Fashion-MNIST: learn on the 60 000 train images, unlabelled;
          evaluate on the 10 000 test images.
Task      find the groups in the data without labels; assign unseen items.
Metric    NMI and ARI of the test assignment against the hidden labels, and
          purity (each group labelled by its train majority).

HeatherDB  competitive-mode database; the train images are streamed in with
           `write` and the memory grows a codebook. MDL picks how many groups
           the codebook warrants (no K supplied). Unseen items are assigned by
           their most-activated hard location (`batch_analyze`, fast read).
k-means    scikit-learn MiniBatchKMeans, given HeatherDB's K (same budget),
           and k-means given the true number of classes (K=10, an oracle
           choice HeatherDB is not given).

recs.doc:
Task 3 - Recommendations, and Task 4 - Freshness (new data -> served).

Dataset   MovieLens 1M (GroupLens). Implicit feedback: a rating is a view.
Split     leave-last-out by timestamp: each user's most recent rating is held
          out; everything else is training data. Evaluated on a seeded
          sample of users (same users for every system).
Task      rank the whole catalogue (seen items excluded) for each user.
Metric    HR@10 and NDCG@10 of the held-out item.

HeatherDB  storage-native, no training step: an item's vector is a fixed
           random projection of the users who watched it (d=128, computed
           from training data); each user's history is written into their
           own collection; the user's `fingerprint` ranks the catalogue.
Popularity most-watched items.
ItemKNN    cosine item-item neighbourhood over the interaction matrix.
ALS        `implicit` AlternatingLeastSquares, 64 factors, 15 iterations
           (the standard matrix-factorisation recommender).
Raw sum    the same item vectors HeatherDB gets, summed with no memory: shows
           what the associative memory adds beyond the encoding.

Freshness  the cost to make a brand-new user's history servable:
           HeatherDB = write that user's collection (one request);
           ALS = refit the model (the usual nightly retrain), timed.

fraud.doc:
Task 5 - Fraud / anomaly detection (the job an outlier-detection model does).

Dataset   Credit-card fraud (ULB/Worldline, OpenML 1597): 284 807 card
          transactions, 492 frauds (0.17 %), 28 PCA features + Amount.
Split     seeded stratified 50/50. Detectors see NO fraud labels: they learn
          "normal" from a 50 000-transaction sample of training normals.
Metric    ROC-AUC and PR-AUC (average precision) on the full test half;
          recall at a 1 % false-positive budget (the usual review-queue cut).

HeatherDB  `bulk_load` the normals (each its own attractor, k=1 read);
           score = 1 - cosine(transaction, fast-read reconstruction). The
           encoding is standardised features plus a constant bias coordinate
           c=100, unit-normalised: for c >> |x|, 1 - cos(a, b) ~ |a-b|^2/2c^2,
           so the cosine read measures Euclidean distance to normal.
IForest    scikit-learn IsolationForest (300 trees), same normals.
LOF        scikit-learn LocalOutlierFactor (novelty, 20 neighbours), same normals.

classify.doc:
Task 6 - Tabular classification (the job a supervised ML model does).

Dataset   Bank marketing (UCI, OpenML 1461): 45 211 customers, 16 attributes,
          target = subscribed to a term deposit (11.7 % positive). The
          canonical churn / propensity / lead-scoring shape.
Split     seeded stratified 70/30.
Metric    ROC-AUC and PR-AUC on the test set.

HeatherDB  classification as associative completion, no model: each training
           customer is stored with its outcome attached (address = customer,
           counter = customer + outcome slots). A new customer is read with
           the outcome slots blank; the read fills them in. Score = the
           positive slot's share of the completed outcome.
LogReg     scikit-learn LogisticRegression (the classic baseline).
GBDT       scikit-learn HistGradientBoostingClassifier (the strong default
           for tabular data; the XGBoost/LightGBM family).

access.doc:
Task 7 - Access control (the job a supervised model on ids does).

Dataset   Amazon Employee Access (OpenML 4135): 32,769 access requests,
          9 categorical id columns (resource, manager, role, department,
          title, family, ...) with up to 7,518 distinct values, mostly rare.
          Target: access granted (94 %).
Split     seeded stratified 70/30.
Metric    ROC-AUC (the dataset's standard metric; PR-AUC is uninformative
          at 94 % positives).

HeatherDB  selective attention with the 9 columns as learned symbol fields:
           requests are written once in random order; each is recalled from
           the requests already stored with its outcome blank, and the miss
           moves attention and the codes of the values involved. Scores come
           from `recall` with the request's values.
LogReg     scikit-learn LogisticRegression on one-hot ids (the classic strong
           baseline for this dataset), C=1.
GBDT       scikit-learn HistGradientBoostingClassifier on ordinal ids.

heather_footprint.estimate_note: peak = the 5-database run measured together + recommendations-symbols run alone (389 MiB) + access (64 MiB, est.)
